title: Along the Ribs of Stone
story:
James followed the ancient masonry of the Old Stone Aqueduct as it marched in a steady, unbroken line across the broad valley floor. The great stone arches rose on either side of him like the ribs of a sleeping leviathan, their moss-draped flanks carrying the musical murmur of clear mountain runoff high above the damp earth. Every fifty paces, James paused to trace the green-felted mortar with a curious finger, listening to the hollow echo of water rushing through the stone channel overhead.

By midday, the aqueduct led him past wide, terraced fields where cornstalks rustled softly in the highland breeze. James had never seen such neat rows of emerald green... James had never felt such rich, damp earth beneath his paws... James had never known a silence so vast and uninterrupted by the rumbling motor-carriages of Oakhaven. He pulled his brass pocket compass from its cord, watching the trembling needle settle steadily southward, pointing toward the deeper green of the southern agricultural flatlands.

As the afternoon shadows began to stretch long across the stonework, James reached a mossy junction where a narrow dirt path branched away from the aqueduct toward a cluster of whitewashed drying sheds. He slipped his compass back into his pouch, adjusted the leather strap of his map canister across his shoulder, and took a quiet breath of the cedar-scented air. Stepping off the stone channel onto the soft soil of the path, he whispered his greeting to the southern expanse.

Pleased to meet you, whatever comes next.
location: A dirt path branching from the Old Stone Aqueduct
